I have also learned to diversify my emergency equipment - I have solar lights, some smaller power stations for usb charging and a small kerosene heater and three kerosene lamps.  Good to be prepared for emergencies or camping trips by taking a couple of these along with a light, a heater and a cooker...just in case!

The rod sock is a bit lacking and the ties just don't do it justice. Upon pulling the rod pieces out and putting them together I can see this is a beautifully crafted rod with no flaws and the feeling of new cork (of course I take the plastic off, who are you saving it for?) against the skin of my hand is luxurious!
I take it outside because I am in a low ceiling room. The action is spot on fast just as I had ordered and just like I like it!
I put the reel on it (of course I had one ready) and take it out back to the trout stream that runs through my backyard, one of the advantages of living in the Smoky Mountains! After I get the line out and make a few false cast I lay my fly right where I want it. This rod cast pretty damned good, I got a hit and miss but it was enough for me to evaluate this rod and write this review.

VEVESMUNDO 50L Hiking Backpack Men Women for Travel Mountaineering Climbing Camping Trekking (Blue) I’ll admit, this is our first hiking backpack, but we are very pleased with the choice. It’s lightweight, but the materials feel solid enough for longevity. it’s comfortable on either of our backs. And it’s got plenty of room. We do a couple hours to half a day hikes/walks and wanted to be able to carry things we want (eating, comfort) as well as for safety (I’m putting together a safety kit). This backpack fits it all.

We’ve been using it just around some smaller area trails - not longer hiking yet - for some days out during Covid and it’s carried a lot of things. We have it filled right now from yesterday’s outing - it worked perfectly. There are plenty of spots/pockets/hooks for carrying in or attaching to. Adjusting the straps to fit each of our bodies was easy and quick.

For beginners or midlevel hikers and day trips just getting around, I think it’s perfect. I can’t speak to hiking pros, but I can’t (currently) see what more you’d need. This has quickly become a go-to for us. We have a day bag, but I see us filling this with extras, keeping it by the door, and grabbing it for a range of days out.

Love the colors (blue with orange) and the material. Love the way it sits. Even fully loaded we were both comfortable, so that was an added plus. We hope to one day get out for longer trips and think this will be a perfect backpack to take us safely into the wilds.

Overall we are very happy with this backpack and happy we chose it.
text_fidelity_b: VEVESMUNDO 50L Hiking Backpack Men Women for Travel Mountaineering Climbing Camping Trekking (Blue)

With only one coffee drinker in the family we didn't need a 3 quart coffee boiler for camp coffee. What we needed was an inexpensive, well built, 3-4 quart container for boiling water for cocoa, making coffee with a a one-cup Melita drip coffee cone, reconstituting instant oatmeal, and for easily adding hot water to our camp showers. The Graniteware coffee boiler was exactly what we needed. We fill it, use what we need for breakfast, then turn it off and set it aside. Later, especially if the day is cloudy or the solar shower water has cooled later in the evening, we'll add some more water, reheat, then add the hot water to our solar showers. We split it between two 2.5 gallon solar showers. The Graniteware Coffee Boiler was exactly what we needed and we've had absolutely no problems. Be sure to use a hot glove or pad when pouring if you just took it off the fire or the stove.

I also use it in my backyard for replenishing water in my smoker. I've learned the temperature of the smoker remains more constant when I add boiling water to the water reservoir. My gas grill has a separate pot burner and it is right next to my smoker. I just fill the coffee boiler with water, place it on the burner, and have hot water at the ready when I need to replenish the smoker.

text_fidelity_a:
Morakniv Companion Heavy Duty Knife with Sandvik Carbon Steel Blade, 0.125/4.1-Inch I have not received my knives yet.
I did go to my local knife shop and handled one before I placed my order.
I handled the Normal mora first. I was impressed with the blade size and quality. At .10 inches thick I thought it was plenty wide for most tasks.
Then I inspected the .125 inches thick Mora of the style I eventually ordered. Wow, the blade was very beefy. The handle has great ergonomics and fit my hand very nice. The blade was hellaciously sharp. Use with caution! The sheath had a very positive retention system that held the knife firmly with no rattling or movement. The sheath belt loops appear very robust and over built. This blade is simple and cheap, but do not underestimate it! The blade would make short work of most butchering tasks. Its long enough to be adequate as a fighting knife. I cant wait till they arrive so I can torture test one to death. I need knives that I can rely on, that can hold up under pretty bad conditions. I need a knife I can depend on for my life. I think I found it! I'll post more when I actually test it out.

***** UPDATE Jan 14th *****

I received my 3 mora knives yesterday. Shipping was very fast. They came packed well in a box. Each knife was in its own sealed ziploc style bag. No documentation besides the shippers receipt arrived with the knives. First thing I did was cut at the box they came in. They were all absurdly sharp but one was a tad sharper than the others. That one is now my EDC (Every Day Carry). I have already added a patina to my EDC and my back up. I have left the third mora bare. I used the boiling vinegar method. Boil vinegar. Degrease blade with rubbing alcohol. Put blade in vinegar for 15 mins. Clean blade to remove residue. Repeat as many times as you need to get the blade as dark as you want. I only did two runs. This treatment will reduce the possibility of rust and corrosion forming on the blade.

I'll be doing some bush-craft in the next few days and putting them through their paces in the kitchen. More to come.
text_fidelity_b: Morakniv Companion Heavy Duty Knife with Sandvik Carbon Steel Blade, 0.125/4.1-Inch

This bike is a completely different experience so my advise would be to practice in a place that's deserted...so here's the low down on my first week of riding on a regular basis....first, this bike will get up and go and reach 20 mph very fast, and for me that was my first surprise, then getting a feel for the 5 levels of resistance 1 being the most and 5 is where you hardly pedal at all, but here's where you need to pay attention....the throttle takes up about half the right handle bar so it's very easy to accelerate when you don't want to so pay attention...then there the issue with the kick stand which seems be very wobblily and a little unstable....having said that, I really like this bike, it's very easy and fun when you get used to it...quick note, I would not leave my house with charger plugged it just to be safe...So now on July 13th or having the bike for over a month the only thing that is driving me nuts is the kick stand...it flops down over and over again even after tightening the so called locking mechanism..it is aggravating and turns my bike ride into a hassle.....it's a terrible TERRIBLE design....................*******.........So I've  owned the bike almost 4 months and I continue to love this bike, I replaced the kick stand and replaced the seat with one a lot more comfortable, The one thing that, for me, makes the ride safer and more predictable is....if I'm riding near people or on roads with intersections I keep the resistance on 1 or 0 and use the hand throttle to provide power to the bike. I used to keep it on 2-4 but found that when I wanted to stop if any pressure was put on the pedals when trying to stop immediately throws the bike forward when you're not expecting it..I learned the hard way and it wasn't pretty..In my opinion controlling the bike with the hand throttle is the safest except if your riding on a trail or on a road with no stop and go...This in my opinion is the best and safest way to operate the bike with the electric assist....aside from that this is a great entry level bike at a very good price.  I look forward to many more miles of fun...

CRKT Halfachance Fixed Blade Parang Machete: 18 Inch Black Powder Coated Carbon Steel Parang Style Blade with Nylon Sheath for Survival, Hunting & Camping K920KKP Back in 1994 when I bought my waterfront property in Southwest Florida the first bid I got to (legally) trim my mangroves was $1,000.00. Even then I thought that the price was outrageous and I decided to do it myself. Needless to say it involves a lot of time and and some really good cutting tools (and skills). There's not a lot of room for maneuvering in the wetlands, the footing is hazardous, the flora and fauna always a challenge (most Florida plants either have thorns or some type of poison), and the bugs can drive you nuts. Now that I think about it, maybe the $1,000.00 would have been money well spent.

Now at age 67 the current bid for the same job is up to $8,000.00. Either the workers are a lot smarter or they don't really want to do this type of work. About 10 years ago I had some major surgery and had to hire three people to do the job for me. When I was watching them the youngest picked up and held a very pretty snake for his father to see, causing me to yell at his father to "put it down". I was really surprised to find out that they didn't know what a coral snake was. That hiring experience also resulted in all of my tools being damaged to the poiint of no return. But the real capper was that they cut the mangroves to a height of 4 feet -- when I had specified 6 feet. Fortunately no one reported me to the mangrove police.

So I have trimmed my own mangroves for 22 of the past 23 years, even at my advanced age. The secret is to keep your eyes and ears open, to use adequate insect repellant and sun protection, wear boots, long pants and long sleeves, and an SPF 50 hat. But the key to being able to trim mangroves for up to six hours at a time is to have a really good medium length machete. This CRKT Chanceinhell(CIH) really fits the bill. It has a durable, heavy and sharp blade, a well-constructed rubber grip for comfort, and a decent sheath that you can hang from your belt when you are using a different tool. This machete is blade heavy which gives you better balance for chopping versus slicing.

When I have the room to swing a machete, I rely on an Esee Lite machete (around $80.00), a blade perfect for slicing thicker wood. For the crowded areas where taking a full swing would be impossible (or foolhardy) I find chopping to be more efficient and safer. That is where the CIH hits the mark and is the best tool to use. You might wonder why I don't use a small chainsaw instead. There are a multitude of reasons: the high noise level masks other sounds that I need to be aware of ( like the movement of snakes, alligators and other critters), chainsaws are dangerous even when operating in the best of conditions (which is far from true in the wetlands), the probability of bounce-back or dropping a running chainsaw is pretty much guaranteed, and trucking in and out of the wetlands to refuel sets you up for additional problems.

So this year I'll be heading into the wetlands with my Chanceinhell and Esee, splitting my time between slicing and chopping, hoping to avoid any injuries. One thing that I can guarantee is that the experience is always interesting.
text_fidelity_b: CRKT Halfachance Fixed Blade Parang Machete: 18 Inch Black Powder Coated Carbon Steel Parang Style Blade with Nylon Sheath for Survival, Hunting & Camping K920KKP

Under Armour Dominate 24 Ounce Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel Bottle with Flip Top Lid Original Review (5 Stars):
I bought a pair of these in Indigo and Silver for my wife and I a couple months ago. We filled them with margaritas and took them to the beach. ;-) They worked beautifully. Now, we used them as overnight water bottles. I fill them about half way with ice then top with water, and they are still icy the next morning, and sometimes even the next day after work (about 18 hours later). The flip-up lid is great for 1-handed use. The little plastic ring, while looking a little weak, has actually stood up very well. The rubber grip and otherwise textured surface makes them easy to hang onto during long walks. I've never had the slightest problem with leaking or spilling. We absolutely love these, and will continue using them daily for years to come.

Update, reduced rating to 3 Stars:
My wife and I have been using these bottles daily for about two and-a-half years. After about a year, both bottles' vacuum seals failed, so water will no longer stay cold overnight, even when filled completely with ice right before bedtime. They also sweat almost immediately after filling. For the price, I'm really not thrilled that these didn't last longer. Further, the seal between the cap and bottle has proven to be less than adequate, as it lets some moisture out into the cap's threads every day. I have an older model Thermos with a screw top which came with a much better seal, that's still good after 5+ years, plus its vacuum seal is still intact despite being dropped several times.

LIGHTBAR | LED Headlamp, 300 to 500 Lumens, Spot Light Mode and Red Light Modes Available On Select Models - Perfect for Camping Running Biking Fishing Construction I've had this for a couple of months, but just used it for the first time this past weekend while camping with friends. I will never use it for that again.

A) The wide angle sounds like a good thing, but it was really annoying to my friends. I had to keep the headlamp at the lowest possible brightness, and even then the light shining so wide was still annoying to everyone around me.

B) The led strip is very thin, resulting in the light source being behind the plane of my glasses. So much light was reflecting off the lenses of my glasses back into my eyes that I truly couldn't see much of anything in front of me. There's no point lighting a path if I still can't actually see the path.

Also, this headlamp has a proprietary charger. So you have to keep that specific single-use cable with you in order to recharge the batteries. And the batteries drain even when not in use. I charged it fully when I first got it a couple of months ago. Fortunately I tested it before my camping trip and discovered it was completely drained. So you can't just charge it and expect it to be ready when you need it. I had to fully charge it just before I left.

It is really very bright, so if you need something really bright, and you don't have glasses, and there's no one else around you who might be blinded by your headlight, then it might be an ok choice for you. But with so very many options out there, I recommend you keep looking. There are definitely better choices than this.
text_fidelity_b: LIGHTBAR | LED Headlamp, 300 to 500 Lumens, Spot Light Mode and Red Light Modes Available On Select Models - Perfect for Camping Running Biking Fishing Construction

text_fidelity_a:
TOURAcademy Home Edition 8-Week Total Golf Improvement Program TOURAcademy's Home Edition 8 Week Total Golf Improvement Program is absolutely the best home program available today for both golfers and beginners at golf. I should start by saying I came from a home where my father paid for lessons for my 3 younger brothers (who all won tournaments as children), but would never pay for me (a daughter). I always wanted to play the game, but never had the time or money over the years raising my own family to get into the game of golf. Now with my children grown, in recent years, my husband, who is a self taught golfer took me to driving ranges and putting greens, where I love to be outdoors learning the game, but without any lessons, failed to have the ability to hit a good shot. A pro who gives lessons came up to me at the driving range and told me, to hit a good shot, I need the basics. He gave me a couple tips and that made me want to learn more. Out of every 50 golf balls I hit, 45 felt like I was hitting a block of cement. My good shots that clicked went about 100 yards, so for a never played the game person, it encouraged me to learn the basics. I bought books and dvd's- but they don't go slow enough or detailed enough for me to learn anything.

This TOURAcademy Home Edition Program is so totally different from any of the programs and books on the market, that I am certain it will help anyone- from young to old, new to a long time golfer. The pro at the driving range told me I don't have the flexibility of a young golfer and that I would have to do what was within my ability, and that is what this TOURAcademy program says as well- get as flexible as you can for your best shots. The program comes with 9 Lesson dvd's covering: 1.) The Set Up-Grip,Posture,Alignment 2.) Rolling It-The Essentials Of Putting 3.) The Impact Zone-Educate The Hands 4.) Learning Small Swings-Chipping 5.) Developing Body Motion-The Pivot 6.) Mastering Intermediate Distances-Pitching 7.) Synchronizing Body & Club-The Full Swing 8.) Power & Distance-Driving With Authority 9.) Specialty Shots-Lob & Bunker.

The TOURAcademy is where the pros practice, and these PGA pros really know their stuff. The dvd's are narrated by 1991 British Open Champ Ian Baker-Finch, a superb golfer. The lessons are given by TOURAcademy's Instructors Travis Fulton, John Stahlschmidt and Christina Lecuyer. What makes this 9 Lesson dvd set so superb are the slow, meticulous detailed lessons. On Disc 1, the grip is shown in details how to begin your set up, by marking your glove and hand with a marker so the club will fit you perfectly. It's this very clear and concise instruction that allows me to learn at my own slow pace. They give you all the exercises to give you the flexibility and right movements to swing properly and remain aligned. It's all so detailed and wonderfully concise, making it easy to copy. I could always putt, but never drive a ball. No one ever told me that you have to hit down to make it hit up. I never wanted to hit near the ground before I got these lessons.

Also included are alignment sticks, which are invaluable in learning your proper stance, swing and where to stand to the ball. For Disc 3, there is a Contact Bag they included for your lesson, which you stuff with towels or an old blanket, so you can practice connecting your club to the right spot on the bag. At the end of each lesson on the dvd's, there are practice white tracks for beginners or blue tracks for golfers wanting to improve their game. And even more included items are a Practice Guide, a Bonus dvd called Troubleshooting- Diagnose Your Swing, Analyze Ball Flight & Extras, an 8 Week Program Calendar and an Instruction Manual.

Practicing with these dvd's brought back a lot of memories of my 3 younger brothers learning golf in the 60's. Instead of hitting this included Contact Bag, my brothers hit a car tire. At my age, I'd break my wrist hitting a tire, so the contact bag is perfect for me. My husband, who is a self taught golfer is actually thrilled with many of the tips for his game- correcting his slice is a huge thing at our age. As for me, I'm learning to hit the ball with a click instead of like a block of cement and that is one step closer for me to get on a golf course. This is the BEST Pro Golf Program I've yet to find with it's 9 detailed dvd's, Bonus dvd, alignment sticks, Contact Bag, Calendar and books. I know from my brothers playing golf all the time, that 8 weeks is just the beginning of learning the basics- the rest is practice all the time to be good. Like the pro's say: If you are not constantly improving your game, you become stagnant, and with this great program giving me all the basics of golf in 8 weeks, I can get ready to practice, practice, practice and finally play the game.
text_fidelity_b: TOURAcademy Home Edition 8-Week Total Golf Improvement Program

The trip by bike is shorter (timewise) that using my car, parking is much easier, and closer to the stores and faster. Sometimes searching for a parking place takes longer than driving to the store.

I mention my location because weather did not factor into my decision grid when selecting cargo carriers on my bike. If I still lived in Seattle I probably would have gone for a rainproof option.

So when I bought my bike I immediately bought a Wald folding basket to attach to my rear rack. The design has several shortcomings but I was able to get it installed using wire ties, rather than the metal clips Wald provided, and it has served my purposes. The mounting hardware Wald provided did not fit the rack on my bike and was not the same color as the basket and my bike. .

When I decided to add a second basket to the other side of the rear rack on my bike I decided to try the Sunlite model because it had a few features I now knew would be valuable (experience with the Wald basket taught me a lot and made me appreciate the reviewer's comments on both products).

Here are the main reasons that I find the Sunlite product to be superior to the wald basket. I have uploaded three photographs that address my reasons for preferring the Sunlite product. The Sunlite basket is on the left on my bike and the Wald one is on the right.

1. The sunlite model is larger when open which benefits cargo capacity.

2. Sunlite thought out the attachment options better and even provided some beefy wire ties as an attachment option. I did not use the provided hose clamps because I thought they would scratch my bike and the black wire ties matched my bike. Sunlite provided a couple of really beefy wire ties but I had to use some of my own to finish the job. More wire ties would be nice.

3. The latch that keeps the sunlite basket closed is much more effective that the one on the Wald. One of the photos I uploaded shows the bungee cord work around I use to keep my wald basket closed when its not in use. In the photo you can see the damage to the finish on the wald basket that was a result of the latch scratching the paint. In the long run the Sunlite latch might not be any better but its starting out as way more effective that the one on the Wald Basket. One of the problems with the Wald latch is that it seems to have been designed for an unpainted basket and the layers of paint on the latch and basked wire makes the latch very difficult to rotate.

4. The mesh bottom on the Sunlite basket keeps my mail from falling through the bottom of the basket. That is a problem with the wald basket when I stop by our mailbox on the same trip to the grocery store.

5, The finish on the Sunlite basket is better than the one on the wald basket.

Both of these baskets handle quite a bit of weight with no problem. I have put three 12 packs of soda in my Wald basket and it has held them secure.

Reviewers for both products have mentioned the fact that you need to bend the outer wall of the basket outward to get the support for the bottom in place. This is mentioned as a disadvantage but I look at that as a feature that assures me that the bottom wont fall out of my basket when Im using it.

The Wald basket is slightly cheaper than the Sunlite but, in my opinion, it is not enough cheaper to justify the Wald over the Sunlite. On the other hand the Wald basket is serviceable enough that I'm not going to replace it with a second Sunlite.
text_fidelity_b: Sunlite Rear Wire Folding Basket

eHUPOO Push Up Bars Parallettes Dip Bars,Strength Training Pushup Stands for Bodyweight Workout&Home Gym Exercise,XL Push Up Stand Bars for Men Women,with Hand Grips Non-Slip Sturdy Structure.24x13” After a few uses my wife and I are both happy to have added this set to our workout options and happy to recommend.

This was a frustrating, but easy set to put together.
First, the pieces are few: the two U bars, 4 bases, screws with washers, little wrench, and 2 hand grips. The hand grips are on, but are velcro so they can be removed and returned.

The set is easy to put together, one person can really do it in about 10 minutes.

That said, it was a but frustrating: having to hold the screw in place while turning the wrench - the little wrench kept sliding off the screw head and there is nothing to hold the other side - other than your hand - to help tighten. It worked, but it took awhile, and it was frustrating. Perhaps using another wrench of your own, but 1. they emphasis not over tightening and use of another tool might encourage that, and 2. I didn’t feel like I needed it in the end. Yes, a little rough, but it worked as is. I would strongly encourage checking tightness from time to time.

I’ve used it a few times and find my weight doesn’t let me do it too much yet, but I’m able to maintain what I do on the ground. I plan to use this intermittently with the ground and another piece of equipment I have. My wife too has used it and with less weight to lift is already able to do both push ups and reverse push ups. It’s a great height, the weight keep it secure - we have used it on living room carpet - and is not at all too heavy to move around. It is a large set, meaning you’ll have to find somewhere to keep it. But it’s not so large as to not be usable.

Overall this is a great set and we are happy to have added it to our workout equipment. This will get great usage and is already contributing to our love of competition. Happy to recommend.

Bodyguard Inverted Umbrella, Large Windproof Umbrellas for Rain & Sun, Compact Umbrella Reverse Umbrella with Reflective Stripe, Teflon Umbrella for Women Men, Travel Folding Umbrella with Cover Bag Every company seems to think that it can make the "next big thing" in umbrellas. It seems as though I've tried dozens of folding umbrellas that promise "this and that" but ultimately fail in one (or more) of the stated advantages. Most have some type of catastrophic failure after only a few uses, some so bad that they make the umbrella totally inoperable. So it was with some skepticism that I ordered this blue Bodyguard Travel Umbrella. It made a lot of promises on its product page -- but would it work as promised?

Finally I've found an umbrella that delivers on its promises. This Bodyguard Travel Umbrella sells for the impressive price of only $20.99, and puts a very useful collapsible umbrella in your hands. You can tell as soon as you pick it up that it is well-made and durable. It has some heft to it, snaps open with the push of a button, and collapses its canopy when you push the 'close' button. Then all you have to do is push the collapsed canopy down into the handle and your compact umbrella can be put into the supplied travel case.

The extra ribs give it additional strength when using it in the wind. It is probably more likely that it would be blown out of your hand than have the umbrella turn inside out on you. The handle is comfortable, fits my hand well, and has a wrist strap to keep it from the aforementioned potential flyaway. Yup, someone finally brought out a good one.

text_fidelity_a:
12 / Pk Deerfly Patches/TredNot Deer Fly Patch Odorless Repellent Ok, you can decide if I'm either stupid or desperate. One of the biggest problems encountered working in my yard during the summer in Southwest Florida are these insanely aggressive deer flies. They bite hard,even through your shirt, but they seem to particularly like your cheek, neck or lips. They don't stop pestering you until they are either able to feed or you manage to kill them. The best method I have found so far is to patiently wait for one to land on you and then beat the crap out of it. The problem is that I encounter several of them every day.

So I fell for this flypaper on a hat deal, hoping against hope that it would work where other methods have failed. I have used it for four hours every day for five days in a row. The results: NOT ONE DEER FLY CAUGHT! They continue to buzz around me and I continue to impatiently wait for them to settle so that I can kill them, but not even one deer fly even managed to trap itself on the flypaper by accident.

The product headline says "Repellent Strips" but also discloses that it contains no chemicals or odors. If the product has no chemical on it, how does it repel the deer flies? The only way I can see this working is by attaching the strips to a tennis racket and swinging it at the incoming deer flies. At least I'd get some more exercise and maybe kill a few before they can bite me.
text_fidelity_b: 12 / Pk Deerfly Patches/TredNot Deer Fly Patch Odorless Repellent

text_fidelity_a:
LaserLyte Laser Sight Center Mass SM Rail The other reviews mentioning the finely threaded battery compartment are pretty accurate. The first thing I did when I got mine was wipe down the threads, there was definitely dust that immediately wiped off that I could see being a problem. After it was cleaned I applied a little bit of mineral oil to the threads (probably something better, but it is what I had), and the screwing/unscrewing was much smoother.

Once I added in the batteries and began screwing the cap back on, I could understand why so many people are worried about it. It is really hard to tell if the resistance you are feeling when screwing it back in is because of the spring on the cap, or because it is not threaded well. If you go carefully it should screw back on fine - especially if you clean the threads and apply a little oil.

The laser seems to function exactly as expected, the strobe mode blinks a little faster than I was expecting, but that is hardly a problem.

Will update once it gets some usage!

UPDATE (2 days later): Well the laser started acting weird... Randomly won't turn on, can't rack a shotgun more than a few times without it turning off - and I wasn't even shooting. I'm actually impressed by just how unreliable it is. Going to roll the dice and get an exchange, but my hopes are not very high at this point.

EDIT: I got a second one of these and am pleased to report that it is more reliable. Was able to put a few dozen rounds thru my shockwave with no issue.

I want to give it 5 stars, but considering the problems so many people have had (myself included) I simply can not.
text_fidelity_b: LaserLyte Laser Sight Center Mass SM Rail

So...55% polyester makes me kind of leery but at the same time realize that it will provide more strength to the sock. BUT....the comfort is out of this world. And the thickness of the sock should be durable for all the sports activities. These socks are reinforced at the heel and toes and have elastic at the top band. All clothing manufacturers put "sizing" on their fabric which gives it a crisp smooth finish. You want to remove this coating especially if you have sensitive skin. text_fidelity_a:
MidTen Magnetic Bore Sight, Red or Green Laser Bore Sight Kit Multiple Caliber, Professional Laser Bore Sighter Rifling Scratch Proof, Suitable for Sighting Scopes Hunting Magnetic Connection Works perfectly magnetized to the end of the barrel. This is obviously for scoped weapons as it's diameter is too large for open sights. If you have a scoped pistol this will work for it as well, otherwise you'll want an actual caliber chamber-fitted bore sight IMO.

This is a no-brainer. No adjustments are available for the laser. It either does or doesn't do the job. To test it, simply place it on a flat level surface and roll it back and forth on the flat. The dot should maintain it's position. If it doesn't, return it for a replacement!

Remember, ALL bore sights are simply to get your rifle or pistol on paper at 25 yards without wasting a box or two of ammo trying to achieve the same result. Once there, fire a few rounds at the desired distance, adjusting your scope each time until it's zeroed in at the yardage you desire.

It doesn't matter that this bore sight isn't perfectly centered, as most aren't anyway contrary to popular belief. Even chamber fitted caliber-specific bore sights aren't perfect and you'll still need to fire a few rounds to be sure your actually sighted and zeroed in at the desired yardage. You can center this by hand on the end of the barrel. It doesn't need to be perfect and will be within a half inch or less of barrel center on target anyway.

At today's ammo prices, this will save you enough in ammo costs and time sighting in so that you'll be able to have more ammo for game or target shooting and put you in the field hunting faster than without one. It's "extremely rare" and I stress, "extremely rare" contrary to the claims here and there that a bore sight zeros you in to that 1/2" group at 100 yards. "Extremely rare". Be prepared to finalize your sighting in at 100 yards to zero with a few rounds after you get on paper.

Be knowledgeable and wise about what a bore sight is designed to do and you'll be happy with your purchase. As long as it gets you on paper so you can see your shot on the paper target in your scope or sighting monocular, the rest is up to you!

Only reason many reviewers leave less than a 5 star rating for this bore sight with few exceptions, is because they don't know how to use it or how to sight in a rifle or pistol in the first place. This is the ONLY bore sight you'll ever need to get your scoped firearms on paper for a good starting point. Like I said, the rest is up to you.

It works! If you don't know the exact procedure to zero your scope in, don't be afraid to ask for help.

I wasn't payed or compensated to state my opinion here. The above opinion comes from understanding what these tools are for, a little logic about what your trying to achieve with them, and a lot of experience. Get some if you don't have any and enjoy your firearm and it's accessories to the best they are capable of performing.
text_fidelity_b: MidTen Magnetic Bore Sight, Red or Green Laser Bore Sight Kit Multiple Caliber, Professional Laser Bore Sighter Rifling Scratch Proof, Suitable for Sighting Scopes Hunting Magnetic Connection

I convinced my husband to try these wheels on the Wonder Wheeler first. We followed the advice of other reviewers and bought a 36" length - 3/8" diameter steel rod from ACE (couldn't find one at Home Depot) and 4 metal flat washers to fit the rod (which would be used as new axle). We drilled a hole 1/2 inch from both ends using a titanium drill bit (the carbide one we bought was useless). We used 1/2" pvc pipe cut to the width of the new wheels. We inflated the tires to 4 lbs. with an electric pump; removed linch pins from original axle (don't lose these or plastic bushings), removed original big plastic wheels, bushings, and axle.
To assemble with new tires: 1) We inserted new axle; 2) then the original bushings (with end protrusion cut off); 3) then a metal washer; 4) new tire with pvc inserted through center; 5) another washer; and 6) inserted original linch pins through drilled holes (repeat steps 2-6 on other side). It now works like a dream and saved us several hundred dollars since we didn't have to buy a new cart.
text_fidelity_b: StoreYourBoard Replacement 12 Inch Balloon Wheels Kayak Dolly and Sand Carts, Big Beach Buggy Inflatable Tires

Super Strong Braided Fishing Line - 4 Strands Multifilament Pe Fishing Line - Abrasion Resistant Braided Lines – Incredible Super Power line 10LB-133LB, 110 Yards-1100 Yards Good line for trolling or jigging. This is an economy version of the spectra superlines that allow you to hold more line and go deeper with less drag and almost no stretch. This line holds knots as well as any of the superbraids, and better than some of the coated, slicker lines.

This probably isn't the best choice for a casting reel. I'd look for an 8-strand line because its a little smoother and should pay out better than this 4-strand braid. The newer coated lines probably cast better, too. For trolling or jigging, though, this stuff works great, especially if you're on a tight budget.

Be sure to check the prices on all the different colors once you've selected the weight of line you want. Sometimes there's a deal on one of the colors that makes it really affordable. You might want to check the prices of larger spools of your selected weight, too. Sometimes you'll find that they've discounted one of the colors in a bulk-size spool that makes it cheaper than the smaller spools of the same weight test. Good luck on the water!

Let me know if my comments are helpful.

I like that it has uses 4 AAA batteries. Devices with 4 batteries USUALLY have very long battery life, in my experience. It appears that all the covers to the buttons and hatches, etc, are water resistant and maybe waterproof. I like the positive slide on-off "click" of the power button. I love that I can leave one 16gb flashcard internal, and plug in a 2nd flashcard, and then without looking at any of the pictures, transfer everything off the 2nd card to the 1st card (assuming there's room), and then put the 2nd card back into the trail camera. That might be this viewer's best feature--the 2 SD card slots feature. The screen is adequate, altho I feel to really look at the pics, you should look at them on a laptop or desktop computer.

OK, here's what I don't like. I don't like the SD card sticking out of the bottom of the viewer. I would rather it be pressed into the slot and catch with the spring-loaded catch like the internal card slot, and be able to completely close the cover on the SD card. BUT, I realize they may have made it that way so you could take the card out with gloves on, cold fingers, etc. I also don't like how that rubber flap kinda hangs in the breeze when I peel it off to insert a card. I don't like how you can't see all the pics on the screen in a matrix (unless I haven't figured that out yet, and if I'm wrong, I will apologize) and choose from them. I don't like how you have to scroll thru the pics. I also think it takes too long to transfer photos from the trail cam card to the internal card.

I know I'm being nit-picky about some of my dislikes, but I still gave it 4 stars. Oh, also, I paid about $65 (with shipping) not on Amazon Prime, because it wasn't available for Prime when I ordered it, and I noticed today that it was about $51 on Amazon Prime from another vendor. text_fidelity_a: KardiaMobile Personal EKG Heart Rate Monitor – 6 Leads - Record EKGs at Home - Detect Irregular Heartbeats and Irregular Arrhythmias - Includes 1 Year Access - Works with Most Smartphones – AliveCor Believe it or not, I still remember, when I was a little girl, that our doctor would make house calls when necessary although back then we didn't call the doctor very often.  Currently, just trying to get a doctor's appointment means you have to look to the future two-four-six months before you can get into their office!  Anything requiring immediate attention seems to be emergency room visits with few in-between choices.  What it seems to me is that we are going to virtual office visits, first with Nurse Practitioners who will refer to Physicians only those cases they feel a doctor should see.  Having this Kardiamobile device, for me, is wonderful as I can monitor my heart rate.  At the present time, I don't seem to be having any issues, but what I really wish is that I could text/email or in some other way send an electronic version of my current record to be added to my medical record.  I mean, at my age, I would think that having a weekly/monthly electronic records (heart rate, O2 sats, sleep-breathing issues, etc) would begin to paint a picture for my doctor that could help him prescribe specific meds and/or tweak others based on these records.  Along with these records, a 10-15 minute Zoom face-to-face with my doctor would be the way of the future.  Still, that may be the next iteration of the app.  For now, printing out my record is the next best thing.  I will say that this little device is something anyone my age or anyone with heart issues should have - easy to use, small enough to carry with you wherever you go and very accurate as well.  Oh, the last thing - I happen to have a couple of small clamshell cases (old harmonica cases) that works well to carry this device, but I would love it if it came with a small case so you have no excuse to leave it behind when you are out of the house...why?  Because that's when your heart issues may flair up and if you can capture that on record, it is an invaluable thing for your doctor to see!  As far as the cost goes, yeah, I wish it was cheaper, but this is SO worth the price!
text_fidelity_b: KardiaMobile Personal EKG Heart Rate Monitor – 6 Leads - Record EKGs at Home - Detect Irregular Heartbeats and Irregular Arrhythmias - Includes 1 Year Access - Works with Most Smartphones – AliveCor

text_fidelity_a:
Vilaxing 50’’ Trampoline with 5 Levels Adjustable Handle Bar for Adults Kids Max Dynamic Load 330lbs Fitness Exercise Workout Rebounder Trampoline for Indoor Outdoor Training I'm going to be honest up front and put this all into perspective: my wife and I have decided (at least for the foreseeable future) to not even bother attempting to put this Vilaxing 50’’ Trampoline with 5 Levels Adjustable Handle Bar together. We have both just spent 8 weeks sick from head colds that became worse. I'm strong guy, but I've had a double ear infection and I'm coming back from that, so weakened and not up to this level of assembly. I want to say that by way of saying, for someone else or for us in a month or so, we would have the strength to do this.... but we talked about it, and I'm not sure we'd even do it then.

This Vilaxing 50’’ Trampoline with 5 Levels Adjustable Handle Bar came 100% disassembled and that alone makes us not want to do it.

We have had 3 previous personal trampolines over the years just like this is supposed to be - we only got rid of them due to moving and once, lack of use. Every single one of those came with the round mesh surface 100% assembled on the frame and only the legs needing to be screwed in, then required tightening from time to time to maintain its safety. You are asking someone to jump repeatedly on something that needs to stay together and endure that kind of pressure.

In this case you have to even assemble the round frame - THEN add the however many links to that - and then maintain it over time. No thanks.

If we'd been in a store and they'd brought out this box to us, we would have known and not purchased. In this case, if we'd bought it rather than receiving it as a part of the Vine Program to review, we would have returned it. As part of the Vine Program we do not have the option to return it, but that also gives us the chance to state that we personally do not feel that for us, this level of assembly is safe enough. We know the level of use we get out of them and to be sure that the main from is safe enough is not something we feel we will get out of the assembly.

So as of this writing, we have decided not to put the time and energy into this Vilaxing 50’’ Trampoline with 5 Levels Adjustable Handle Bar, something that needs to stay together while you jump on it repeatedly. I'm not going to give it a 1 star as we feel others might feel fine putting in the effort and feeling comfortable with the outcome, and get use out of it. But for us, it's a no-go out of the box. We've put it on a shelf in the garage. We want our equipment safe and while I get some assembly is at times required - in the right ways - this alone made our decision for us. This gets 3 stars for horrible assembly while giving way to the idea others might not find it as dangerous.
text_fidelity_b: Vilaxing 50’’ Trampoline with 5 Levels Adjustable Handle Bar for Adults Kids Max Dynamic Load 330lbs Fitness Exercise Workout Rebounder Trampoline for Indoor Outdoor Training
